clue.text: Poor Edith Shaw has suicidal tendency

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so the two names are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A gloomy remark about a person called Edith Shaw who is feeling self-destructive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' shuffles the ten letters of EDITH and SHAW, leaving 'has' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A longing for one's own death is exactly a suicidal urge.

clue.text: Conduct, under Mao, eastern revolution

indicators.note: a revolution overturns things, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Behaviour under Chairman Mao during the Chinese revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' rearranges UNDER, MAO and E together.
explanation.definitionFit: One's bearing or behaviour, how one conducts oneself.

clue.text: Part of official loan for Scots town

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of a government loan goes to a town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft defined 'for Scots town', but 'for' is only a link joining wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is a town in central Scotland on the River Forth.

clue.text: Naturally they provide residential accommodation

parts.note: reads like housing provided as a matter of course, but means the homes nature provides for wild animals and plants

explanation.surface: Of course they provide places to live.
explanation.definitionFit: The natural surroundings where a species lives are its home environment.

clue.text: Annoyance makes one right about the girl's name

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right goes round the girl and the name

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated at being corrected about a girl's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container, with the right abbreviation enclosing the girl and the name; the 's of girl's is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that irritates is a source of annoyance or vexation.

clue.text: Hesitates to indicate those with property on both sides of the river

indicators.note: the word for property owners sits either side of the river letter, enclosing it

parts.note: the haves are those who own things, as in haves and have-nots

explanation.surface: Someone dithers about showing who owns land on each bank of the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Havers is Scots for to talk nonsense or dither.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots and northern English use havers for dithering or babbling.

clue.text: In Scotland, not a shilling for VIP

parts.note: na is the Scots word for no or not
bob was slang for one shilling in old British money

explanation.surface: A Scots remark that an important person is not worth even a shilling.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, a twentieth of a pound, nicknamed a 'bob'.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a wealthy Indian governor, the word came to mean any rich or important person.

clue.text: Number blown up in Tyne disaster

indicators.note: something blown up is shattered, so these letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A count of something destroyed in a catastrophe on Tyneside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninety is a cardinal number, nine tens.

clue.text: Girl 'put on undergarment at home — flighty thing!

parts.note: bird is British slang for a girl
a bra is a woman's undergarment
in means at home

explanation.surface: A girl dresses in her underwear at home, a scatterbrain.
explanation.definitionFit: A feather-brained, silly person, as giddy as a bird.

clue.text: Rubbish found in ship's bottom

definitions.meaning: the lowest inner part of a ship's hull where water collects

explanation.surface: Junk discovered in the hold of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means nonsense and also the hull's lowest compartment, where foul water gathers.

clue.text: Turn right to left in Forster's hill for the coast of India

indicators.note: the clue tells us to change an R (right) into an L (left) in the word that follows

parts.note: the Marabar Hills and caves are the setting of E. M. Forster's novel A Passage to India

explanation.surface: Directions for a traveller in Forster's novel heading towards the Indian coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Changing the first R of MARABAR to L gives the name of India's south-western coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Malabar is the name of the south-west coastline of the Indian subcontinent.

clue.text: Opening artist left on the upper side

parts.note: a vent is an opening or outlet
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Describes an artist's opening on the left of an upper floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The word usually means belly-side, but in botany the ventral face of a leaf is its upper surface, which is the sense used here.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany the ventral surface of a leaf faces up, towards the stem.

clue.text: Notice a point to alter

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a public notice

explanation.surface: An instruction to note that one detail needs changing.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt something is to modify or change it to suit new conditions.

clue.text: Spinner holds the record

parts.note: sounds like a sports headline about a bowler with a record, but describes the rotating platter of a gramophone on which a disc sits

explanation.surface: A cricket spin bowler holds a record.
explanation.definitionFit: The revolving plate of a record player carries the disc while it plays.

clue.text: Going round it in boring fashion

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters of the two words are reshaped

explanation.surface: A complaint that something is circling in a dull way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... fashion' tells us to rearrange IT and BORING; 'in' joins the fodder words and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite circling the earth is said to be in orbit, travelling round it.

clue.text: Sweetheart well up with university student — lovely!

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend or sweetheart

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: fit means well, in good health
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A lover gets emotional about a university student who is gorgeous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FIT into TIF.
explanation.definitionFit: Attractive and pleasing to look at, as a synonym.

clue.text: Has rockfish a voice?

definitions.meaning: a ... is a fish, and the rock ... is one kind

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a spiny food fish and the deepest male singing range.

clue.text: In Germany fine Viennese composer reveals his master

parts.note: schön is German for beautiful or fine
Alban Berg was a Viennese composer

explanation.surface: A Viennese composer living in Germany reveals who his teacher was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' refers back to Berg: Arnold Schönberg taught Alban Berg, so the composer's name hides his teacher's.
explanation.definitionFit: Schönberg was the teacher of Alban Berg, so he was Berg's master.

clue.text: Honour little Beatrice — she's on her own as egg-producer

definitions.text: she's on her own as egg-producer

parts.note: in bridge the queen is one of the honour cards
Bee is a pet form of Beatrice

explanation.surface: A girl named Beatrice is honoured as a unique mother figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The honours in bridge are the ace, king, queen, jack and ten.
explanation.definitionFit: In a hive only the fertile female lays eggs; the rest of the colony does not.

clue.text: Forged outcrop 'of debit vouchers

parts.note: a spur is a ridge jutting out from a hill
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debt

explanation.surface: A rocky outcrop made of fake debt notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Counterfeit and false, not genuine.

clue.text: Hinder the Admiral?

definitions.meaning: read as an adjective, more hind, at the back
a ... admiral is a naval officer rank

explanation.surface: A question whether someone should obstruct the admiral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hinder' looks like a verb meaning obstruct, but is the adjective 'further back'.
explanation.definitionFit: Back or hindmost describes the first sense; the second completes the rank title of a flag officer.

clue.text: The funny little humpback is in drink

parts.note: rum is old-fashioned British slang for odd or funny
Mr Punch, the hunchbacked puppet of Punch and Judy shows

explanation.surface: A small hunchbacked comic figure is drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch and Judy is a traditional British seaside puppet show whose hero, Punch, has a hump.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed alcoholic beverage made with spirit, fruit juice and spice.

clue.text: Appearing sheepish, but knowing about Common Market

indicators.note: the word for knowing goes round the European trade group

parts.note: fly is British slang for sharp or knowing
the EEC, European Economic Community, was called the Common Market

explanation.surface: Looking embarrassed, though well informed about the European Community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheepish' suggests embarrassed, but here it means like a sheep's woolly coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolly like a sheep's fleece, hence literally sheep-like in look.

clue.text: Arch 23 dn

parts.note: the other entry is the adjective meaning of the foot, so this is the arch of the foot

explanation.surface: A cross-reference: an arch of the kind named in another clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The arched upper middle part of the human foot.

clue.text: Film character in new clean-up shows peevishness

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other
new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of the hyphenated word

parts.note: ET is the alien from Spielberg's film E.T.

explanation.surface: A film star's bad temper shows during a fresh tidy-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' scrambles the hyphenated word, and 'in' tells us the film alien goes inside the result, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sulky irritability or bad temper is what this noun names.

clue.text: Kind of bike to sell, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the word meaning sell is heard, and the spelling of its twin is entered

parts.note: to peddle is to sell wares

explanation.surface: A question of what sort of bicycle someone is trying to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedal bike is one driven by the rider's feet, unlike a motorbike.

clue.text: Pole at home to French artist

parts.note: a rod is a pole or staff
in means at home

explanation.surface: A Polish visitor at home with a French painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality, but it is the rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was a French sculptor, the maker of The Thinker.

clue.text: For a huntswoman, it's a help mounting

indicators.note: in a down entry mounting means climbing upwards, so the words are written in reverse

parts.note: an aid is a help

explanation.surface: Something useful when a huntswoman climbs on to her horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' reverses AN AID; Diana is the Roman goddess of hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana, Roman goddess of the chase, was the archetypal huntress.

clue.text: Turn off left in desert

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the word for desert

parts.note: to defect is to desert one's side

explanation.surface: Directions to turn left off the road into the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a sandy place, but is the verb meaning abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: To divert something from its course is to turn it aside.

clue.text: Rich fabric robe cad pulled to pieces

indicators.note: tearing the words apart and putting them back in a different order

explanation.surface: A scoundrel tore an expensive robe to shreds.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy silk cloth woven with a raised pattern, often in gold thread.

clue.text: Sweet-tin?

definitions.meaning: a confection on a stick, a lollipop

explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang both for a sweet on a stick and for cash.

clue.text: Force to serve squash to the mob

parts.note: to press is to squash
a gang is a mob

explanation.surface: Telling someone to make a drink by squeezing fruit for the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squash' suggests the British fruit cordial, but is the verb crush.
explanation.definitionFit: To coerce someone into service, as navy press gangs once did to sailors.
